meta.problem: Design a norm and incentive layer for an open ecosystem of independent labs sharing hypotheses publicly. Herding increases monoculture. Duplicate effort decreases collective discovery rate. Unretracted errors prevent reliable reuse.

elites.title: Adoption Step-Down Ledger
elites.description: Each public hypothesis carries a live adoption meter. Every independent replication confirmation nudges the meter up by one unit, and labs earn credit for each confirmation. When the meter crosses a crowding threshold, or a falsification finding is posted, every adopting lab's committed budget on that hypothesis automatically steps down by a fixed fraction. The freed effort is routed to rival hypotheses, and a lab that retracts promptly and moves early to a rival earns extra credit, so labs lose nothing by backing away from a crowded or refuted idea.

mechanism.core_mechanism: Confirmations steadily raise lab uptake of a hypothesis, and either crowding or a public falsification triggers a multiplicative cut in commitment, which keeps monoculture and duplicated effort from forming and spreads effort over rival hypotheses.

elites.title: Quarantine-Before-Pile-On: Flag-Triggered Credit Holds with a Correction Interval
elites.description: When a lab posts a hypothesis, early followers normally collect a surge of attention credit, which pulls many labs into the same replication. Any independent lab can file a stake-backed anomaly flag. Once enough flags accumulate, the hypothesis enters a quarantine hold: new follow-on work on it earns no credit or funding priority, so the pile-on is actively suppressed. During the hold, the authors have a fixed correction interval to fix or defend the claim. If they do, the hold lifts and they earn a bonus. If they don't, a binding retraction stamp is issued automatically and propagates to every dependent result. Labs then reuse only claims that were either cleared or cleanly retracted.

mechanism.core_mechanism: Credible anomaly flags earn a temporary hold that withholds credit from herd-style follow-on replication, creating a protected interval in which authors must correct or face an automatic retraction, so that only cleared claims enter the reusable commons.

elites.title: Cooling-Off Hold: An Earned Brake on Bandwagon Replication
elites.description: When an independent lab files a replication-failure report against a trending hypothesis, a discrepancy audit is triggered. If the audit confirms a credible discrepancy, the hypothesis gets a public cooling-off hold. The hold pauses the funding boosts, citation-credit multipliers, and pre-registered replication slots that a surge of attention would otherwise unlock. During the amendment grace period the originating lab can fix or defend the claim, and auditors earn reputation for each flaw they surface. If the flaw is not fixed by the deadline, a binding retraction is issued and downstream labs are notified. Labs therefore experience a visible, time-limited pause on the claim and are not drawn into a pile-on.

mechanism.core_mechanism: A confirmed replication-failure report earns a cooling-off hold that suppresses bandwagon replication during an amendment grace period, so the claim is either fixed or retracted before many labs build on it.

elites.title: Scheduled Audit Sweeps That Release Time-Locked Divergent Hypotheses
elites.description: Labs lodge time-locked preregistered hypotheses, including deliberately contrarian ones, in a vault that stays hidden. When critiques pile up and a funder-triggered audit call arrives, a Correction Sweep runs. It retracts or expires flawed claims, strips credit from imitation cascades that formed around popular claims, and frees their credit slots in the niche registry. Only then does the vault unlock. A lab sees its dormant divergent hypothesis become claimable in a freshly cleared niche, with no crowd already clustered on the old consensus.

mechanism.core_mechanism: A periodic audit sweep, fed by accumulated critiques and triggered by a funder call, both unlocks vaulted divergent hypotheses and suppresses herding on popular claims, so a burst of diverse, non-duplicated work starts in cleared niches.

elites.title: Sealed Commitment Ledger with Runner-Up-Anchored Credit
elites.description: Each lab privately gauges its confidence in a hypothesis and its capacity to pursue it, then files a sealed commitment stating both, hidden from other labs until a window closes. When the window closes, the most committed lab gets the lead-pursuit slot. The credit it can earn, and the retraction liability it carries, are set by the runner-up's filed stance, not its own. Overstating, hedging or copying the crowd therefore gains the lab nothing, because its own filing never sets its terms. Labs do best by filing exactly what they believe, and the public record ends up with honest confidence levels and less duplicated work.

mechanism.core_mechanism: Because the lead lab's credit and liability are anchored to the runner-up's filed stance rather than its own, the pull toward hedged or crowd-mimicking filings is removed, so honest confidence is the best strategy.

elites.title: Audit Shadow: Crowd-Scaled Adversarial Review That Diverts Labs From Herd Claims
elites.description: A rotating, funded corps of adversarial auditors is reinstated and is paid for each verified flaw. Their attention scales with how many labs pile onto the same hypothesis cluster. A lab sees a public audit-exposure meter on every crowded claim. Labs that would have joined the bandwagon redirect toward under-explored hypotheses, where novelty-weighted credit is available. The payoff comes from the monoculture lock-in with uncorrected errors that never forms. Minority lines mature without being swamped, and the pool of verified, reusable results regains diversity.

mechanism.core_mechanism: Audit exposure that rises with crowd concentration makes herding costly, so labs divert before monoculture lock-in forms, and under-explored hypotheses can mature into verified reusable results.

elites.title: Runner-Up-Anchored Confidence Stakes
elites.description: Before sharing a hypothesis, each lab files a public confidence stamp from 0 to 100. The most confident lab gets the lead-replicator slot and funding priority. Its credit if the claim holds, and its liability if the claim is retracted, are pegged to the next-most-confident rival's stamp, not its own. A lab therefore gains nothing by inflating its stamp, and it gains nothing by hedging toward the crowd's consensus. The lab simply reports what it believes, and the stamps show reviewers where real disagreement and real overlap lie.

mechanism.core_mechanism: Pegging a lead claimant's credit and liability to the runner-up's stamp, not its own, removes the payoff from hedging toward consensus, so labs disclose calibrated confidence, which reduces herding and duplicate effort.

elites.title: Additive Endorsement, Multiplicative Standing Cut
elites.description: Each independent reproduction of a hypothesis adds a small, fixed increment of public standing, so trust builds slowly and linearly. When a lab files a credible refutation, the claim's standing is cut by a fixed fraction, and so is the credit of dependent claims and of labs still piling onto it. Labs see their stake in a crowded claim fall sharply on refutation, so they move toward under-explored alternatives, which carry pre-registered replication bounties funded from the cut standing.

mechanism.core_mechanism: Standing grows by small steps with each independent reproduction, while a credible refutation triggers a proportional standing cut that keeps a popular claim from locking in the whole ecosystem and pushes labs toward a diverse, correctable knowledge base.

admitted.title: Probation Board with Bounty-Paid Break-It Sweeps
admitted.description: Every newly posted claim lands on a capped probation board, where labs see how many others are already working on it. When the board crosses a fill threshold, a short randomized sweep pays labs bounties to replicate or refute the claims that have drawn the most attention. Claims that break are retracted publicly and the refuters get credit. Claims that hold graduate to a trusted registry, so labs that avoided the crowd and verified something less visible are rewarded too.

mechanism.core_mechanism: Frequent, cheap, bounty-driven adversarial sweeps triggered by probation-board crowding retract the many claims that fail early, which keeps herding and duplicate effort from building up and lets the few sound claims graduate to a trusted registry that labs can reuse.

admitted.title: Lottery Reserve Cohort with Audit-Triggered Re-expansion
admitted.description: Each funding cycle, a small random fraction of labs is drawn by lottery into a reserve cohort. These labs receive guaranteed baseline credit for developing off-consensus hypotheses and do not pile onto the trending claim. When a community-wide error audit sweep runs, credit for heavily herded claims collapses in proportion to how many labs piled on, but reserve labs hold no stake in those claims and lose nothing. After the sweep, the reserve labs' hypotheses are the seeds for the next round of work, and they earn a premium for being the verified fallback.

mechanism.core_mechanism: A random reserve cohort is deliberately kept out of the herd, so when an audit sweep collapses credit for crowded claims, the cohort is shielded from that collapse and can re-seed diverse, verified research afterward.

admitted.title: Escrowed Claims, Scheduled Audit Sweeps, and Herd-Credit Expiry
admitted.description: Labs lodge hypotheses in a timestamped escrow vault with committed predictions, while critiques from the community pile up in a public backlog. At scheduled audit windows, a review sweep works through the backlog and does three things. It lifts the embargo on the escrowed claims, voids the stacked citation credit that accrues to bandwagon-following, and vacates attention slots on the public board. Labs then see freshly cleared slots and independent replication credit instead of crowd-following credit, so they spread across the claims being released rather than piling onto the loudest one.

mechanism.core_mechanism: A scheduled audit window combined with a backlog of public critiques triggers a sweep that releases escrowed claims while preventing the bandwagon citation cascade, so freed attention slots are filled by a diverse wave of independent replications.

admitted.title: Crowd-Scaled Audit Bounties with Niche Credit
admitted.description: When a hypothesis starts attracting many labs, an open red-team bounty on it grows with the number of labs piling on, so labs that join the herd without independent evidence risk public exposure. Labs therefore hold back from crowded claims and take up neglected hypotheses. admitted.title: Quarantine-Before-Pile-On: Flag-Triggered Credit Holds with a Correction Interval
admitted.description: When a lab posts a hypothesis, early followers normally collect a surge of attention credit, which pulls many labs into the same replication. Any independent lab can file a stake-backed anomaly flag. Once enough flags accumulate, the hypothesis enters a quarantine hold: new follow-on work on it earns no credit or funding priority, so the pile-on is actively suppressed. During the hold, the authors have a fixed correction interval to fix or defend the claim. If they do, the hold lifts and they earn a bonus. If they don't, a binding retraction stamp is issued automatically and propagates to every dependent result. Labs then reuse only claims that were either cleared or cleanly retracted.

mechanism.core_mechanism: Credible anomaly flags earn a temporary hold that withholds credit from herd-style follow-on replication, creating a protected interval in which authors must correct or face an automatic retraction, so that only cleared claims enter the reusable commons.
mechanism.affected_system: Incentive and norm layer (reputation, credit, coordination and correction mechanisms) for a decentralized public hypothesis-sharing ecosystem of independent research labs
mechanism.payoff: Reliably Reusable Result Commons

admitted.title: Lottery-Held Reserve Labs with Audit-Triggered Credit Clawback
admitted.description: When a hypothesis starts trending, a public lottery randomly assigns a small fraction of interested labs to a deferral slot. These labs agree not to build on the trending claim for a fixed window, and in return they get a small guaranteed credit stipend and a reserved funding line for alternative approaches. A public replication audit then sweeps the trending claim. Labs that rushed in lose credit on their derivative work if the claim fails, while the deferred labs are untouched and are first in line to rebuild the area with different approaches. The deferred labs' verified results become the reusable base.

mechanism.core_mechanism: A random, compensated deferral of a few labs keeps them out of the bandwagon, so when a replication audit penalizes crowd-chasers they are shielded from the penalty and can rebuild the field's reusable knowledge.
mechanism.affected_system: Incentive and norm layer (reputation, credit, coordination and correction mechanisms) for a decentralized public hypothesis-sharing ecosystem of independent research labs
mechanism.payoff: Continuity of Reusable Verified Knowledge
